items.q: According to the ITIL definition, can a single person be an organization?
o: Yes, if the person has their own functions with responsibilities, authorities and relationships to achieve their objectives
No, an organization must have at least two people
No, an organization must be a registered company
Only if the person employs staff
items.x: ITIL defines an organization as a person or a group of people with its own functions, responsibilities, authorities and relationships to achieve its objectives. A sole trader can be an organization.

items.q: Whose value should a service provider consider when making decisions?
o: All relevant stakeholders', such as consumers, employees, partners, shareholders and society
items.x: Value is created for many stakeholders. Good product and service management considers the value for all relevant stakeholders, not only the paying customer.

items.q: An IT department's 'new starter' offering includes a phone that the employee keeps, access to the corporate network, and set-up of the employee's accounts by technicians. Which element is a SERVICE ACTION?
o: Set-up of the employee's accounts by technicians
items.x: Service actions are activities performed by the provider for the consumer, such as setting up accounts. The phone is goods and network access is access to resources.

items.q:
Which of the following are parts of a service relationship?
1. Service provision
2. Service consumption
3. Service relationship management
4. PESTLE analysis
items.x: A service relationship includes service provision, service consumption and service relationship management. PESTLE is a model for analysing external factors.

items.q:
Which two of the following are OUTPUTS?
1. A monthly invoice is produced
2. Customer satisfaction improves
3. An incident ticket is closed
4. The company's revenue increases
items.x: Outputs are deliverables of activities, such as an invoice or a closed ticket. Improved satisfaction and higher revenue are results that outputs help to enable.

items.q: Apart from the subscription price, which of the following is a cost IMPOSED on a consumer adopting a new SaaS application?
o: Buying servers to host the application
Paying for data-centre electricity for the application
The effort to integrate the application with existing systems
Hiring administrators to patch the application's servers
items.x: Integration effort is a cost the consumer takes on by using the service. Servers, electricity and server administration are costs that the SaaS service removes.

items.q: A company uses a managed security monitoring service. Which is a risk that the service REMOVES?
o: The provider's own staff misusing access to the company's systems
The provider failing to renew its contract
Attacks going undetected because the company lacks skilled security analysts
items.x: The service reduces the risk of undetected attacks caused by a lack of in-house skills. Misuse of access by the provider's staff, contract failure and tool dependency are risks introduced by using the service.

items.q: Which pairing is CORRECT?
o: Utility = fit for use; warranty = fit for purpose
Utility = fit for purpose; warranty = fit for use
items.x: Utility is fitness for purpose: the functionality that meets a need. Warranty is fitness for use: assurance that agreed requirements, such as availability, capacity, security and continuity, will be met.

items.q: Replacing a faulty network switch with a new model in the data centre is BEST described as what?
items.x: Replacing a component that could affect services is the addition, modification or removal of something with a potential effect on services, so it is a change. It should follow change enablement.

items.q: Which statement about SLAs and experience level agreements (XLAs) is CORRECT?
o: SLAs often focus on technical performance, while XLAs focus on the experience and outcomes people perceive, and the two can be used together
XLAs replace the need for any technical measurement
SLAs are agreements between two suppliers
XLAs only apply to external customers
items.x: Combining technical service levels with experience-based measures gives a fuller picture of whether services really create value, and helps avoid the 'watermelon effect'.

items.q: A manager requests a new laptop for an employee who starts next week. How should this be classified?
items.x: Requests for the provision of a resource, such as a laptop, are pre-defined service requests that are a normal part of service delivery.

items.q: ITIL (Version 5) discusses quality in terms of several aspects that need to be balanced. Which list BEST reflects these aspects?
items.x: Version 5 asks organizations to balance utility (what it does), warranty (how well it performs), experience (how people perceive the interaction) and sustainability (environmental, social and economic impact).

items.q: An organization moves from separate technical teams to cross-functional product teams that share responsibility for outcomes. Which dimension is MOST directly affected?
items.x: Organizational structures, roles, responsibilities and team design belong to the organizations and people dimension, although such a change will also affect how value streams flow.

items.q: Which question is MOST relevant to the information and technology dimension?
o: What information will the product manage, and which technologies are needed to support it?
Which suppliers will provide parts of the product?
Who is accountable for the product's outcomes?
In which order are the workflow steps performed?
items.x: The information and technology dimension asks what information and knowledge are needed and managed, how they are protected, and which technologies support the product or service.

items.q: Which question is MOST relevant to the partners and suppliers dimension?
o: What competencies do our staff need?
How do we protect customer data?
Which workflow steps can be automated?
What is our sourcing strategy for this product, and which external organizations are involved and on what terms?
items.x: The partners and suppliers dimension covers relationships with other organizations, sourcing strategy, contracts and agreements, and how suppliers are integrated.

items.q: Which question is MOST relevant to the value streams and processes dimension?
o: Which cloud provider should we use?
How do the activities and workflows combine to deliver value to the consumer?
What is the budget of the governing body?
items.x: The value streams and processes dimension defines the activities, workflows, controls and procedures, and how they are organized and coordinated to create value.

items.q: A company obtains a partner's capability to provide 24/7 user help (1). The partner then answers users' questions and restores service when issues occur (2). Which lifecycle activities do 1 and 2 BEST match?
items.x: Obtaining capabilities, including people and supplier services, is Acquire. Helping users and restoring normal operation is Support.

items.q: A team compares several cloud providers, selects one and negotiates the commercial terms. Which lifecycle activity is this?
items.x: Acquire obtains the components needed, whether technology, supplier services or people, including evaluating options, selecting suppliers and agreeing terms.

items.q: A defect found while operating a live product leads to rework in Build, followed by a new Transition. What does this show about the lifecycle?
o: The lifecycle is non-linear, and work can move between activities in whatever order is needed
The lifecycle has failed and must be restarted from Discover
Defects should never be fixed once a product is live
Build must never happen after Operate
items.x: Activities are interconnected, and work flows between them as needed. Moving from Operate back to Build and Transition is normal in an iterative lifecycle.

items.q:
Which two lifecycle activities are MAINLY concerned with running a live product and assisting its users?
1. Operate
2. Discover
3. Support
4. Design
items.x: Operate keeps the live product running to agreed targets, and Support helps users and restores normal operation. Discover and Design come earlier in shaping a product.

items.q: Which question MOST helps a team understand the consumer's perspective of value, as recommended by 'focus on value'?
o: What does the service help consumers to achieve, and what costs and risks does it involve for them?
How many staff does the provider employ?
Which supplier has the lowest price?
items.x: Understanding why consumers use a service, what it helps them achieve, and its financial consequences and risks is central to applying 'focus on value'.

items.q: After a merger, an organization objectively assesses the practices of both companies before deciding which ones to keep. Which guiding principle is MOST directly being applied?
items.x: 'Start where you are' recommends assessing the current state objectively, here of both organizations, and reusing what works instead of assuming one approach is always best.

items.q: A team ranks its planned iterations so that the one delivering the most value comes first, and re-plans after each one based on feedback. Which guiding principle is being applied?
items.x: Iterations should be prioritized by value and re-evaluated as feedback arrives. This keeps the initiative focused and adaptable.

items.q: Managers decide to buy more servers to speed up delivery, but cannot see that most delays are actually caused by work waiting for approvals. Which guiding principle would MOST help avoid this kind of decision?
items.x: Insufficient visibility of work leads to poor decisions. Making the flow of work visible shows the real bottlenecks, here the approvals rather than server capacity.

items.q: While improving incident handling, a team looks at the whole value stream from user report to resolution, including supplier hand-offs, knowledge, tools and training, instead of only its own steps. Which guiding principle is being applied?
items.x: Optimizing one team's steps in isolation can shift problems elsewhere. Considering the whole value stream and all four dimensions is 'think and work holistically'.

items.q: 'Use outcome-based thinking to produce practical solutions that deliver valuable outcomes' is MOST closely associated with which guiding principle?
items.x: 'Keep it simple and practical' uses outcome-based thinking and the minimum number of steps needed to achieve an objective.

items.q: Which statement about automation is CORRECT according to 'optimize and automate'?
o: Automation should only be used for simple tasks
Automation is valuable only when it removes all people from a process
Automation can range from simple repetitive tasks to complex decisions using algorithms and AI, but it should follow optimization
Automation should always come before optimization
items.x: Automation can be applied to frequent, repetitive tasks and also to complex decision-making, for example with AI. It should come after simplification and optimization, and be measured with agreed metrics.

items.q: Which statement about the evaluate, direct and monitor governance activities is CORRECT?
o: They form a continuous cycle, in which the results of monitoring inform further evaluation and direction
They are performed once, when the organization is founded
Only one of them needs to be performed in any year
They are performed by the service desk
items.x: Governance is ongoing. The governing body evaluates, directs through strategy and policy, monitors performance and conformance, and then evaluates again as circumstances change.

items.q: Who is ultimately accountable for ensuring that an organization's use of AI complies with laws and regulations?
items.x: The governing body is accountable at the highest level for performance and compliance, including compliance in the use of AI. Responsibilities can be delegated, but accountability remains at the top.

items.q: Why is the baseline created in 'Where are we now?' important?
o: It replaces the need for a vision
It is only needed for audits
It allows the results of the improvement to be measured objectively later
items.x: Without an objective starting point, an organization cannot show whether an improvement has worked. The baseline is compared with results in 'Did we get there?'

items.q: A team considers whether to buy a new tool, retrain staff or redesign a workflow in order to reach its improvement targets. Which step of the continual improvement model is this?
items.x: 'How do we get there?' explores options and defines the improvement plan, which can be a single initiative or a series of iterations.

items.q: Which statement about continual improvement is CORRECT?
o: Improvements should consider all four dimensions, not only technology
Improvements should focus only on processes
Improvements should only be made after major incidents
Only improvements to tools are part of continual improvement
items.x: Improvement opportunities exist in organizations and people, information and technology, partners and suppliers, and value streams and processes. A holistic approach gives better results.

items.q: What is the role of management practices in the ITIL value system?
o: They are used only by external suppliers
They provide sets of resources and capabilities that are used across lifecycle activities and value streams to perform work
items.x: Practices are sets of organizational resources designed for performing work or accomplishing an objective. They are combined within lifecycle activities and value streams to create value.

items.q: What is the purpose of the IT asset management practice?
o: To restore service as quickly as possible
To plan and manage the full lifecycle of all IT assets, helping the organization maximize value, control costs, manage risks and support decisions about assets
To set business-based service level targets
items.x: IT asset management covers assets from planning and acquisition through operation to retirement and disposal. It supports value, cost control, risk management, decision-making and compliance.

items.q: Which statement about the guiding principles within the ITIL value system is CORRECT?
o: They apply only to new projects
They are universal and enduring, and guide decisions and actions throughout the value system
They must be applied in numerical order
They change whenever the organization changes its strategy
items.x: Guiding principles apply in all circumstances, regardless of changes in goals, strategies, type of work or management structure, and they guide behaviour across the whole value system.

items.q: Which statement BEST describes what happens within the ITIL value system?
o: Opportunity and demand trigger activities that, supported by practices and guided by principles and governance, create products and services that enable value
Demand is turned directly into profit without any activities
Only the governing body performs activities
Value is created only during the Build activity
items.x: The value system turns opportunity and demand into value through lifecycle activities and practices, guided by principles and governance, and continually improved.

items.q: A value stream handles well-understood, repeatable work in which cause and effect are clear. Which approach is MOST appropriate?
o: Continuous experimentation with no fixed procedures
Waiting for a crisis before acting
Standardized procedures and established good practice, possibly automated
items.x: In ordered contexts, standard procedures and good practice work well and are good candidates for automation. Complex contexts need experimentation and adaptation instead.

items.q: A value stream has a lead time of 20 days, but work is actively done on it for only 6 hours. What does this MOST likely indicate?
o: The value stream is highly efficient
The team needs to work faster on each task
The process time is too long
Most of the lead time is spent waiting, so improvement should focus on queues, hand-offs and approvals
items.x: When process time is a small fraction of lead time, flow efficiency is low. Reducing waiting, hand-offs and unnecessary approvals usually improves lead time far more than working faster.

items.q: A virtual agent holds natural-language conversations with users to understand and answer their questions. Which capability of the ITIL AI Capability Model is MAINLY demonstrated?
items.x: Communication covers how AI interacts with humans and other systems, for example through conversational interfaces. Coordination orchestrates tasks and workflows.

items.q: Which statement about ITIL and other frameworks and methods is CORRECT?
o: ITIL must be used on its own, without other frameworks
ITIL is designed to be adopted and adapted, and can be used together with approaches such as Agile, DevOps, Lean and PRINCE2
Other frameworks are only allowed for software development
Using other frameworks invalidates ITIL certification
items.x: ITIL provides adaptable guidance that is intended to work alongside other approaches, combining their strengths to co-create value.
